conventions.values: Scores and rates are fractions in [0, 1]; dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only the month is known).
conventions.introduced: Date of the first public version (arXiv v1 where there is a paper).
conventions.best_published: Highest score found in the cited source on the date in 'accessed'; 'date' is when that score was published or listed, null when the source does not say. Settings differ between sources (shots, chain of thought, judge), so best_published is a level, not a comparison.
conventions.label_error: rate = fraction of test items with a wrong or unanswerable reference; the ceiling used by eval-suites-lifecycle is 1 - rate. Definitions differ per source (see 'definition').
conventions.stage: Stage on the compilation date: introduced, climbed, saturated or replaced (section 18.5).

stages.symptom: the benchmark separates models and every model scores low

example.evidence: Seven frontier models score 3.3% to 9.1% on the 3,000-question v1 (best: o1, 9.1%; DeepSeek-R1 9.4% on the text-only subset), Table 1.

stages.symptom: the best published score rises quickly

example.evidence: At release the strongest GPT-4 baseline reaches 39% (experts 65%, 74% discounting clear mistakes); in July 2025 Epoch AI measures Grok 4 at 87% (+-2%) on the Diamond subset, past the expert baseline.

stages.symptom: top scores bunch below a ceiling set by label errors

example.evidence: o3-high reaches 93.3% (OpenAI simple-evals); 6.49% of MMLU questions are estimated to contain errors, so the ceiling is about 93.5%.

stages.symptom: a harder successor restarts the cycle

example.evidence: MMLU-Pro raises the options from four to ten and adds reasoning-focused questions; accuracy drops by 16% to 33% compared to MMLU (abstract).

held_out_tier.design: a private held-out set kept by the maintainers in addition to the public questions, to assess overfitting and gaming on the public benchmark

held_out_tier.scores_quote: At this time, we do not report any model performance metrics on the private held-out set.

fresh_test_set.finding: Accuracy drops of up to 8%; the Phi and Mistral families show systematic overfitting across almost all sizes, while many frontier models show minimal signs of it.
